registry_disposition.reason: S5 Path-Confinement Closure (owner ticket of 2026-10-21), a bounded closure of the path-confinement finding that the HO-01 lane's independent review reached by reproducing it against the shared S5 evaluation module and deliberately named rather than repairing, because that module is the S5 lane's surface. The S5 corpus loader in scripts/tools/run-skill-effectiveness-evals.mjs resolved every corpus-declared path LEXICALLY, so a family file that is a symbolic link out of the corpus directory, a family file reached through a symlinked parent directory inside the corpus, and a corpus directory that is itself a symbolic link out of the repository (CLI --corpus) all carried the evaluation out of the corpus the run is supposed to measure. The loader now confines every declared path to the corpus directory in REAL terms and binds every read to a verified file descriptor, through the new shared primitive scripts/tools/path-confinement.mjs, which proves containment twice and binds the read: C1 the declared path is relative and stays lexically inside the base; C2 the REAL path of the target stays inside the REAL path of the base, so a symlink inside the base that points out and a symlinked parent directory that carries the target out are both refused; C3 the content is read through a descriptor opened with O_NOFOLLOW and O_NONBLOCK on the verified real path, and the descriptor's device and inode identity and the parent directory's identity are compared with the identities observed during the check, so a target REPLACED in the window is detected instead of read and a FIFO swapped in cannot block the open; C4 the target must be a regular file, so a directory, a FIFO or a device can never be read as material; C5 the target must carry exactly one link, so a hardlink, which shares its inode with another name and whose real path is its own path, is refused rather than read. The CLI additionally requires the corpus directory to RESOLVE inside the repository and re-anchors it after the load. The manifest is validated instead of crashing on a malformed one, so a family can no longer be dropped from the measurement silently and leave the security gate passing with zero security cases measured. The corpus error vocabulary keeps CORPUS_PATH_ESCAPES_ROOT for a declared path that leaves the corpus and adds CORPUS_PATH_SYMLINK_ESCAPE, CORPUS_PATH_NOT_A_FILE, CORPUS_PATH_MULTIPLE_LINKS, CORPUS_PATH_CHANGED, CORPUS_MANIFEST_INVALID and CORPUS_VARIANTS_INVALID. The TOCTOU residual is documented and NOT claimed as eliminated: an in-place rewrite of the same inode is not detected, a concurrent writer that replaces the parent directory between the containment check and the open and carries a file with the same device and inode identity is detected as long as the new parent has a fresh inode - the parent directory's own identity is re-verified - and escaping it needs the parent's inode number to be reused as well, which is not detectable without openat(2) relative to a trusted directory descriptor, a hung filesystem can still block in the kernel, and a bind mount inside the corpus is not detected. No CONTRACT_RECORD, PROVENANCE or SUPERSESSION class changes: core/contracts/behavioral-eval.schema.json is untouched, the behavioral-eval validator is untouched, the corpus content is untouched, the BehavioralEvalRecord format is untouched, nothing is superseded, and the evaluation output is digest-neutral (measured: the pristine origin/main tree and this branch produce byte-identical corpus digests, content digests and family digests, and an identical HO-01 comparison record). The runner is a tool surface, not a registered contract. The slice was written against origin/main 2f94f8c5eab6ae3216b9dd0551a03624a88fd55c and rebased onto origin/main 808bfb09175084a90f1eb264fb18e72e9bda0f82 before publication, a base adaptation whose only conflict was the CHANGELOG, where both lanes entries were kept; the loader merged automatically and carries both the S8 producer fix and this slice confinement. Two pre-existing drifts on the base this slice was written against - the HO-01 comparison record failing E13, and the committed S5 eval records no longer reproducing from the corpus - were named and measured by this run and repaired by the S8 evidence-provenance lane in the meantime, not by this one. One cross-lane adaptation was required by the stricter loader: the S8 evidence-provenance module loads the S5 corpus through it, so a corpus file that leaves the corpus is now refused one layer before that module own containment proof could report it, and the module was adapted to keep its specific EVIDENCE_CORPUS_CONTENT_ESCAPES for the same defect instead of its generic corpus-invalid code. The gate caught the shadowing: the S8 lane own test failed on the rebased branch and passed on the pristine base. Per the consumer binding in AGENTS.md, NO_CHANGE requires no Registry write; the change registration for this run is projected separately in the Unitera Registry, and the representation in the Unitera Atlas, after the source merge. The slice was reviewed in two rounds and by a third, independent reviewer. Each review ran on a model different from the one that wrote the slice, with one independent confirmer per finding, every finding re-reproduced by that confirmer from its evidence alone: the first round confirmed thirteen findings and refuted one, the re-review of the repaired state confirmed fourteen (eleven distinct, three reported by both lenses) and refuted none, and the codex connector on pull request 59 raised one further P2 (inode identities must be compared as bigint, or a 64-bit device or inode above Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER can round two distinct identities to the same number and defeat the replacement guard). Every confirmed finding was repaired in the same change, and the outcome is recorded in full in the run record, section 6, with each finding and its disposition. No independent human approval is claimed.
